title: Tune Into the Five Lead Indicators of Team Health
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece identifies five subtle, forward-looking 'lead indicators' of team health that predict trouble before it shows up in lagging metrics like engagement scores or attrition. The five are speed of response between team members, the ratio of clarifying questions asked, how openly mistakes are acknowledged, how broadly credit gets distributed, and the frequency of unsolicited help or ideas offered outside formal roles. Each indicator is explained with a short description of what healthy versus struggling teams look like. The piece closes by noting these signs decline months before performance problems become visible, giving leaders a chance to intervene early.
points: Lag indicators like engagement scores and attrition trail team problems; lead indicators appear earlier.
The five lead indicators are speed of response, ratio of clarifying questions, mistake acknowledgment, credit distribution, and unsolicited contributions.
Healthy teams distribute credit broadly and volunteer help outside formal roles without being asked.
These signals typically decline months before performance metrics show any sign of trouble.
quotes: Lead indicators are earlier, more subtle signs that predict whether a team is about to thrive or struggle.
Highly cohesive teams respond quickly to each other and do not let the status of leaders or other team members influence this response pattern.
Teams that will struggle to execute now and in the future stop asking clarifying questions before launching an assignment or making a decision.
The best teams and team members are quick to acknowledge mistakes and often flag them to others to begin conversations about improvement.
Strong and healthy teams distribute credit more broadly, and those that struggle have a narrower distribution.
Lead indicators reflect the future of a team’s dynamics months before strengths and weaknesses appear.
